intro: Practice Active Directory tasks in a simulated console, and test your knowledge with matching and ordering tasks.

labs.title: Handle tickets in Active Directory Users and Computers
labs.summary: Work three help desk tickets in a simulated ADUC console: unlock an account, put a new hire in the right groups and offboard a leaver.
labs.scenario:
Three tickets are in your queue for corp.example.com:

  1. Priya Shah (pshah) is locked out after typing her password wrong. She has been verified. Unlock her account.
  2. Marcus Webb (mwebb) is a new accountant. His account exists but is disabled. Enable it, place it in the Accounting OU and make him a member of Accounting-Users and VPN-Users.
  3. Dana Ortiz (dortiz) left the company today. Disable her account, move it to the Disabled Users OU and remove her from VPN-Users and Sales-Users. Do not delete it.

Group membership is shown as one Yes/No column per group. Edit the table, then Save changes. Don't change anyone else.

tasks.text: pshah is unlocked, still enabled and in her groups
mwebb is enabled and in the Accounting OU
mwebb is in Accounting-Users and VPN-Users only
dortiz is disabled and in the Disabled Users OU (not deleted)
dortiz is removed from VPN-Users and Sales-Users

hints: Locked out is a separate column from Enabled.
Group membership is one Yes/No column per group.
Leavers are disabled and moved, not deleted, so you can recover data and meet retention rules.
labs.solution: pshah: Locked out No. mwebb: Enabled Yes, OU Accounting, Accounting-Users Yes, VPN-Users Yes. dortiz: Enabled No, OU Disabled Users, VPN-Users No, Sales-Users No. Save.
labs.review: Unlock for lockouts, enable for new hires, and disable-and-move for leavers. Match access to the person's role through groups, and never delete an account on the day someone leaves.

labs.title: AD building blocks
labs.summary: Match AD terms, order the GPO processing and AGDLP, and fill in ports and commands.
labs.scenario: Review the basics before your first week on the help desk.

activities.title: Term to meaning
activities.prompt: Drag each description to its term.

items.text: Server that authenticates users and stores the directory
Container used to organize objects and apply policy
Top-level security boundary with a shared schema
A set of settings linked to a site, domain or OU
Searchable partial copy of every object in the forest

activities.title: Group Policy processing order
activities.prompt: Order from first to last applied.

activities.title: AGDLP
activities.prompt: Order the steps of the group strategy.
items: Put user accounts in Global groups
Put Global groups in Domain Local groups
Assign permissions to the Domain Local group

rows.label: Command that forces a Group Policy refresh
PowerShell cmdlet that unlocks an account

hints: Local, Site, Domain, OU: the last one wins.
labs.review: Know the structure (forest, domain, OU), the policy order, AGDLP, and the ports and commands you will use daily.
